ns2:section.sectionText: Black representation in television has a long history that is both positive and problematic. Studies in Black TV explores how black television remains deeply relevant in popular culture and amidst a changing media landscape. This course explores two general questions for contemporary television viewers: How are Black people represented in television? Can television aid consumers in cultivating and developing a critical consciousness about race and Black experience? During the course we explore critical tools for grappling with stereotypes and positive representation through the lenses of race, gender, and class. By surveying Black television from the 70s through today spanning various genres, the course invites students to map similarities and differences in Black families, relationships, politics, and cultural life.
